informational.rule: area "dir" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: dir/** matches a file below the directory
cases.why: `**` matches any number of segments.

informational.rule: area "dir" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: dir/** matches the directory itself
cases.why: A pattern that ends in `/**` also matches the path before `/**`.

informational.rule: area "dir" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: dir/** matches the directory itself without case
cases.why: The directory rule is case-insensitive like the rest.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: dir/** does not match a longer name
cases.why: The directory name must match as a whole segment.

informational.rule: area "star" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: * matches inside one segment
cases.why: `*` matches any run of characters except `/`.

informational.rule: area "star" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: * matches an empty run
cases.why: `*` may match nothing.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: * does not cross a slash
cases.why: `*` never matches `/`.

informational.rule: area "middle" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: **/ in the middle matches zero directories
cases.why: `a/**/b` matches `a/b`.

informational.rule: area "middle" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: **/ in the middle matches several directories
cases.why: `a/**/b` matches `a/x/y/b`.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: **/ in the middle needs a whole segment
cases.why: `pkg/**/test` does not match `pkg/xtest`.

informational.rule: area "leading" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a leading **/ matches at the root
cases.why: `**/name` matches `name`.

informational.rule: area "leading" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a leading **/ matches at any depth
cases.why: `**/name` matches `a/b/name`.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a leading **/ still anchors the segment
cases.why: `**/.env*` does not match `x.env`.

informational.rule: area "question" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: ? matches one character
cases.why: `?` matches exactly one character.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: ? does not match zero characters
cases.why: `?` matches exactly one character.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: ? does not match two characters
cases.why: `?` matches exactly one character.

informational.rule: area "class" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a class matches a listed character
cases.why: `[abc]` matches one of the listed characters.

informational.rule: area "class" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a class matches without case
cases.why: A class is case-insensitive like the rest of the pattern.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a class does not match another character
cases.why: `[abc]` matches only the listed characters.

informational.rule: area "range" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a class with a range matches inside the range
cases.why: `[0-9]` matches one digit.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a class with a range does not match outside the range
cases.why: `[0-9]` matches one digit.

informational.rule: area "negated" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a class negated with ! matches another character
cases.why: `[!abc]` matches one character that is not listed.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a class negated with ! does not match a listed character
cases.why: `[!abc]` matches one character that is not listed.

informational.rule: area "caret" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a class negated with ^ matches another character
cases.why: `^` at the start of a class negates it, as `!` does.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a class negated with ^ does not match a listed character
cases.why: `^` at the start of a class negates it, as `!` does.

informational.rule: area "unclosed" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a [ with no ] is a literal character
cases.why: A class that is not closed matches the character `[` itself.

informational.rule: area "negated-empty" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: [!] matches a slash
cases.why: The `!` counts as the first character of the class, so `[!]` is a negated class with no members, which matches any one character.

informational.rule: area "negated-empty" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: [!] matches a line feed
cases.why: A negated class with no members matches a line terminator too.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: [!] does not match zero characters
cases.why: A class matches exactly one character.

informational.rule: area "caret-empty" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: [^] matches a slash
cases.why: `[^]` is the same as `[!]`.

informational.rule: area "negated-slash" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a negated class with members matches a slash
cases.why: `[!a]` matches every character that is not `a`, `/` included, so `t[!a]x` crosses a directory boundary.

informational.rule: area "range-slash" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a class whose range holds the slash matches a slash
cases.why: `[.-0]` is the range from `.` to `0`, which holds `/`.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: ? does not match one character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane
cases.why: `?` matches one UTF-16 code unit, and U+1F600 is two.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a negated class does not match one character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane
cases.why: A class matches one UTF-16 code unit, and U+1F600 is two. The sixth open question of the README records the behavior.

informational.rule: area "triple-dir" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: *** before a slash matches zero directories
cases.why: A run of three or more `*` is the same as `**`, so `tri/***/x` matches `tri/x`.

informational.rule: area "triple-dir" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: *** before a slash matches several directories
cases.why: A run of three or more `*` is the same as `**`.

informational.rule: area "triple-inner" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: *** inside a segment crosses slashes
cases.why: A run of three or more `*` is the same as `**`, so `a***b` matches across `/`.

informational.rule: area "range-upper" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a range matches the other case of a letter that it holds
cases.why: `[@-Z]` holds `A`, so it matches `a` without case.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a range does not match a character between the two cases
cases.why: `[@-Z]` does not hold `_`, and `_` has no other case. The ends of a range are not folded, so `[@-Z]` is not `[@-z]`.

informational.rule: area "range-mixed" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a range whose ends differ in case is in order
cases.why: `[A-_]` runs from U+0041 to U+005F, so it is in order, and it matches `a` because it holds `A`.

informational.rule: area "negated-then" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: [!]x] is [!] followed by x and ]
cases.why: The class ends at the first `]` after its first character, so the rest of the glob is literal.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: [!]x] does not match one character
cases.why: `[!]x]` needs three characters.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a class whose first character is ] does not match that character
cases.why: The reference reads `[]` as a class that matches nothing, so the glob matches no path. The second open question of the README records the behavior.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a class whose first character is ] does not match its other member
cases.why: The reference reads `[]` as a class that matches nothing, so the glob matches no path. The second open question of the README records the behavior.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a class whose first character is ] does not match its own text
cases.why: The reference reads `[]` as a class that matches nothing, so the glob matches no path. The second open question of the README records the behavior.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: []] does not match ]
cases.why: The reference reads `[]` as a class that matches nothing, so the glob matches no path. The second open question of the README records the behavior.

informational.rule: area "inner-stars" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: ** inside a segment crosses slashes
cases.why: `**` that is not a whole segment matches any run of characters, including `/`.

informational.rule: area "trailing-stars" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: ** at the end of a segment crosses slashes
cases.why: `build**` matches `build-out/x`.

informational.rule: area "normalized" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a pattern is normalized like a path
cases.why: A leading `./` and a repeated `/` in a pattern are removed.

informational.rule: area "literal" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: other punctuation in a pattern is literal
cases.why: `+`, `(`, `)`, and `.` match themselves.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a . in a pattern does not match any character
cases.why: `.` is not a wildcard.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: ** does not match a line feed
cases.why: `**` matches any run of characters except the four line terminators.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: ** does not match a carriage return
cases.why: `**` matches any run of characters except the four line terminators.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: ** does not match U+2028
cases.why: `**` matches any run of characters except the four line terminators.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: ** does not match U+2029
cases.why: `**` matches any run of characters except the four line terminators.

informational.rule: area "dir" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: ** matches U+0085
cases.why: The next line character is not one of the four line terminators.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: ** inside a segment does not match a line feed
cases.why: The rule for line terminators holds for `**` in every position.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: **/ in the middle does not cross a directory with a line feed in its name
cases.why: The directories that `**/` matches hold no line terminator.

informational.rule: path is in no area; writes are denied by default

cases.name: a leading **/ does not cross a directory with a line feed in its name
cases.why: The directories that `**/` matches hold no line terminator.

informational.rule: area "star" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: * matches a line feed
cases.why: Only `**` excludes the line terminators. `*` excludes only `/`.

informational.rule: area "question" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: ? matches a line feed
cases.why: Only `**` excludes the line terminators. `?` excludes only `/`.

informational.rule: area "negated" write is granted to role dev

cases.name: a negated class matches a line feed
cases.why: Only `**` excludes the line terminators.

description: The policy glob dialect. The role may write every area, so a result of allow with an area means that the pattern of that area matched, and deny means that no pattern matched.
